name: Modern Java (21+)
description: Enforces Java 21+ features including records, sealed classes, pattern matching, and virtual threads.
content:
# Modern Java (21+) Rules

- Use `record` for immutable data carriers — no boilerplate getters, equals, hashCode, toString
- Use `sealed` classes and interfaces to restrict inheritance hierarchies and enable exhaustive pattern matching
- Use pattern matching with `instanceof` — replace manual casting with `if (obj instanceof String s)`
- Use switch expressions with pattern matching and `when` guards for cleaner branching logic
- Prefer virtual threads (`Thread.ofVirtual()`) for I/O-bound tasks instead of platform thread pools
- Use text blocks (`"""`) for multi-line strings — SQL queries, JSON templates, HTML fragments
- Use `var` for local variables when the type is obvious from context — keep readability paramount
- Prefer `Optional` over null returns — never call `.get()` without `.isPresent()` or use `.orElse()`
- Use `Stream.toList()` instead of `.collect(Collectors.toList())` for unmodifiable lists
- Prefer `SequencedCollection` interface methods (`getFirst()`, `getLast()`) over index-based access
- Use `String.formatted()` or `STR` template processor instead of `String.format()` for interpolation
- Avoid `synchronized` blocks — use `ReentrantLock` or structured concurrency with `StructuredTaskScope`
